findings.rationale: GA's observed outcome prevalence (0.294) is well above what its features imply (mean predicted 0.170), giving CITL -0.12 (z -7.8) and ECE z +5.3, with AUC normal (0.809). The same direction shows in both sex subgroups (O/E 1.81 and 1.63). Its update norm is the largest in the federation (median ratio 2.5, z +6.3) and grows steadily from about 0.2 in round 1 to about 2.8 in round 20. This is what persistent label-feature mismatch produces, not sign-flipping: cosines average near zero. Per-round prevalence is elevated from round 1 (0.23 in round 1, roughly 0.22-0.35 thereafter).

MI shows observed prevalence (0.243) above predicted risk (0.164), CITL -0.079 (z -5.2), with AUC normal (0.808). Its Sex=1 subgroup has O/E 1.43 (z_noise 5.3). Its update norm rises from about 0.5-0.8 in rounds 1-3 to about 3.0 by round 20 (median ratio 2.29, z +5.4), with cosines near zero. The pattern is weaker than GA's, so this is a moderate-confidence finding.

CT shows observed prevalence (0.203) above predicted risk (0.133), CITL -0.070 (z -4.5), with AUC normal (0.798). Both sex subgroups have O/E above 1.4 (z_noise 4.2 and 5.4). Its update norm stays near 0.5-0.9 through round 7, then rises to about 1.4-2.2 from round 8 (median ratio 1.83, z +4.4). The evidence is several moderate signals, not one extreme one, so confidence is low.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients across updates, performance, drift, features and three subgroup attributes, then used the remaining budget to examine per-round behaviour of the strongest candidates. The clearest fault is GA: its outcome prevalence runs well above what its features imply (CITL z -7.8), its AUC is normal, and its update norm grows steadily from round 1. This fits prevalence_shift from round 1. MI and CT show the same pattern with weaker evidence (prevalence above prediction, update norms rising from about round 5-8), so I report them at moderate and low confidence. Label noise is not fully excluded for MI and CT, since AUC alone does not separate it from prevalence shift. No subgroup under-diagnosis (O/E below 1) was found, and no drift, missing-sentinel, free-rider or poisoning signature was confirmed. Other outliers (NC GenHlth tail, ND HighChol spread, NV and GU drift, DC BMI, scattered binary-feature p99 values) were not confirmed by a second tool. The budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
